options.C: Bargaining
options.D: Anger

explanation: Bargaining involves trying to negotiate a different outcome or postpone the inevitable loss. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h2)

question: Besides stopping ovulation, how does progestin help prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By creating an electrical charge in the uterus
options.B: By neutralizing the natural acid levels in the vagina
options.C: By increasing the temperature of the vaginal canal
options.D: By making the cervical mucus thick and hostile

explanation: Progestin changes the consistency of cervical secretions into a thick barrier, making it way too hard for sperm to swim through to meet an egg. Neat, right?

question: Why do intrinsic sugars digest much slower than free sugars?

options.A: They bind to red blood cells and delay energy release
options.B: They are protected by the natural cellular structure and fiber of the food
options.C: They bypass the stomach and enter the small intestine immediately
options.D: They require no digestive enzymes to break them down into glucose

explanation: Because the fiber and cell walls are intact, your digestive system has to put in extra work. This slows down how fast sugar enters your bloodstream, giving you steady energy!

question: What is an adverse event?

options.A: A natural progression of a chronic disease without any medical intervention
options.B: Any intentional harm inflicted on a patient by a healthcare provider
options.C: An injury caused by medical care rather than the patient's underlying illness
options.D: A patient refusing to take their prescribed hospital medications

explanation: Adverse events specifically refer to unintended injuries caused by healthcare management rather than the disease itself. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of primary prevention for unintentional injuries among adolescents?

options.A: Prescribing antidepressants after a deliberate self-harm episode
options.B: Providing physical therapy following a severe motor vehicle crash
options.C: Suturing a deep laceration in the emergency treatment room
options.D: Conducting community road safety education and enforcing helmet laws

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention stops injuries from happening in the first place through safety education, proper rules, and policy enforcement.

question: What gland releases follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone?

options.A: Posterior pituitary gland
options.B: Hypothalamus
options.C: Anterior pituitary gland
options.D: Adrenal cortex

explanation: The anterior pituitary gland responds to signals from the hypothalamus by secreting follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h1)

question: What is an effective way for a nurse to uncover a patient's hidden fears?

options.A: Assuming the patient is fine if they do not complain
options.B: Waiting until the doctor makes the primary diagnosis
options.C: Checking only the temperature chart every four hours
options.D: Asking open-ended questions about their current concerns

explanation: Spot on! Asking open questions like 'How are you feeling about everything?' gives patients a safe space to share worries they might otherwise hide.

question: If a nursing mother's diet lacks enough nutrients, how does her body manage to produce breast milk?

options.A: The body absorbs extra nutrients directly from the air
options.B: Milk production stops completely until diet improves
options.C: The body draws from maternal stores to maintain milk
options.D: Breast milk loses all its essential nutrients instantly

explanation: Nature makes sure the baby gets what it needs! If diet falls short, the mother's body will use its own stored nutrients to keep the milk flowing. Great job understanding maternal priority!

question: What is the standard baseline daily protein recommendation (RDA) for a healthy, less active adult?

options.A: 10 grams per kilogram of body weight
options.B: 5.0 grams per kilogram of body weight
options.C: 0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight
options.D: 2.5 grams per kilogram of body weight

explanation: 0.8 grams per kg is the golden baseline set to keep a healthy adult from deficiency and maintain a steady nitrogen balance. Easy to remember for your exams!

question: Why must nurses stress to parents the importance of finishing a child's entire course of antibiotics?

options.A: To prevent the child from developing a skin rash
options.B: To permanently boost the child's daily appetite
options.C: To completely wipe out the bacteria and prevent relapse
options.D: To ensure the child gains healthy weight rapidly

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early just because the child 'looks better' can let hidden bacteria bounce back and cause more kidney damage. Patient education at its finest!

question: Which option best describes true informed consent in clinical research?

options.A: An agreement signed by the hospital manager on behalf of the patients
options.B: A verbal promise made by the researcher that no complications will occur
options.C: An ongoing, voluntary dialogue ensuring participants understand risks and rights
options.D: A quick signature obtained by a doctor right before a surgical procedure

explanation: Informed consent isn't just a one-time signature. It's a continuous conversation making sure the participant is fully aware and knows they can walk away anytime. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h4)

question: What triggers the sudden mood swings and emotional shifts right after childbirth?

options.A: The total exhaustion of red blood cells in the brain
options.B: An abnormal buildup of carbon dioxide in brain tissue
options.C: A sudden increase in thyroid hormone production by the liver
options.D: The rapid drop in placental hormones like estrogen and progesterone

explanation: You've got this! Delivering the placenta causes a sudden drop in hormones, which can temporarily rock the nervous system and cause emotional ups and downs.

question: Why must you cross-check delivery notes with actual physical supplies before paying a vendor?

options.A: It guarantees that the supplier will offer a discount on the next order
options.B: It automatically updates the expiration dates of the received medications
options.C: It prevents paying for items that were billed but never actually delivered
options.D: It satisfies the legal requirement for filing annual income taxes

explanation: Always count what's in the box! Checking physical goods against the invoice protects the hospital from paying for items that were left out or short-supplied.

question: Why does blood from an upper GI bleed usually turn black and tarry (melena) by the time it comes out?

options.A: The patient has been eating too many dark green vegetables
options.B: Bile acids in the large bowel bleach the blood
options.C: Stomach bacteria turn the iron bright red
options.D: Digestive enzymes and stomach acid break down the blood during its trip

explanation: As old blood travels all the way down the long digestive tract, stomach acid and enzymes break down the hemoglobin, turning it dark, sticky, and black.

question: Over time, how does chronic, untreated high blood pressure harm the heart?

options.A: By permanently dilating all major veins in the lower extremities
options.B: By thinning the heart muscle walls and causing extreme hypotension
options.C: By eliminating the need for peripheral vascular resistance
options.D: By injuring arterial walls and causing left ventricular hypertrophy

explanation: Fighting against high pressure everyday makes the heart muscle work out too hard—just like lifting heavy weights, it gets bulky and thick (hypertrophy), which isn't good for it long-term.

question: Which of these is an example of paralanguage during a patient interaction?

options.A: The medical diagnosis written on a chart
options.B: The physical distance between you and the bed
options.C: The volume and speed of your voice
options.D: The hand gestures used while explaining a procedure

explanation: Paralanguage refers to vocal qualities like pitch, speed, and volume that accompany spoken words. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h1)

question: What is the best imaging test to check for liver hydatid cysts?

options.A: Electrocardiography
options.B: X-ray fluoroscopy
options.C: Ultrasound
options.D: Positron emission tomography

explanation: Ultrasound is safe and brilliant at spotting fluid-filled cysts hiding inside the liver.

question: Why is communication in IEC a two-way process rather than a one-way lecture?

options.A: It is required by government policy for every primary health center.
options.B: It ensures that nurses do not have to speak during health outreaches.
options.C: It allows healthcare providers to listen to community fears and local beliefs.
options.D: It stops patients from asking difficult questions about medications.

explanation: Great nursing is all about listening, not just talking! Two-way communication helps us understand what people are really going through so we can help better.

question: What is the very first thing the nursing team must do if a swab count doesn't add up?

options.A: Ignore the discrepancy if only one small gauze is missing
options.B: Discharge the patient and file an incident report later
options.C: Inform the surgeon immediately and halt closure
options.D: Wait until the patient wakes up to ask them

explanation: Never keep quiet about a wrong count! Alert the surgeon right away so nobody gets closed up with an extra item inside.

question: Why must a patient finish their entire course of anti-parasitic medication?

options.A: To prevent the medication from expiring in the home medicine cabinet
options.B: To avoid the development of chronic high blood pressure
options.C: To build permanent immunity against all future parasite strains
options.D: To ensure the parasite is completely eradicated and prevent recurrence

explanation: Stopping medication early is like leaving a few weeds in a garden—they'll just grow right back! Finishing the dose ensures every last parasite is gone.

question: In community nursing, how do we best describe a "community"?

options.A: A single hospital ward with patients and staff
options.B: A collection of medical doctors working in one clinic
options.C: Every person living within a country's capital city
options.D: A group of people sharing values, interests, or geography

explanation: Spot on! Think of a community as people connected by bonds, shared spaces, or common goals—not just four hospital walls. You're getting the hang of this!

question: What does "interdependence" mean in a community?

options.A: The government controls every aspect of private family life
options.B: Members and subgroups rely on each other for survival and support
options.C: Foreign countries manage all local health clinics
options.D: Every single household produces all its own food and medicine

explanation: Interdependence means people and groups lean on one another to make daily life work smoothly.

question: Your patient stands on their tiptoes to grab a chart from a high shelf. What foot movement are they doing?

options.A: Dorsiflexion
options.B: Inversion
options.C: Plantar flexion
options.D: Supination

explanation: Correct! Pointing your toes downward toward the floor (like pressing a car gas pedal or standing on tiptoes) is plantar flexion.

question: Why must a nurse always wear gloves when applying topical medications to a patient?

options.A: To warm up the cream before it makes direct contact with the patient's body
options.B: To prevent the patient's natural skin bacteria from contaminating the medication tube
options.C: To keep the patient's room environment completely sterile during the procedure
options.D: To protect the nurse from accidentally absorbing the medication through their own skin

explanation: Many topical drugs are potent and can easily pass through the nurse's fingertips into their own bloodstream if gloves are omitted. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h6)

question: What is a fomite in the context of infection control?

options.A: A specialized mask used for airborne disease isolation
options.B: A living insect that carries parasites to humans
options.C: An inanimate object that can transmit infectious agents
options.D: A chemical spray used to clean hospital floors

explanation: Fomites are non-living surfaces or objects like stethoscopes or tables that hold onto germs and pass them along. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h3)

question: What is the primary protein that makes up human hair?

options.A: Fibrin
options.B: Elastin
options.C: Collagen
options.D: Keratin

explanation: Hair is built primarily from a tough, fibrous structural protein known as keratin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h1)

question: A diabetic patient is stressed because they cannot afford their monthly insulin. Who should the nurse involve first?

options.A: Radiology technician
options.B: Surgical specialist
options.C: Social worker
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: Brilliant! Social workers are absolute rockstars at connecting patients with financial aid and community assistance programs.

question: What is the primary focus of a strategic plan in nursing management?

options.A: Immediate treatment of a single patient
options.B: Broad, long-term organizational goals
options.C: Ordering supplies for the current week
options.D: Daily shift scheduling and staff breaks

explanation: Strategic plans look years ahead and focus on the big-picture mission and direction of the entire healthcare facility. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which enzyme found in saliva starts the chemical breakdown of carbohydrates?

options.A: Trypsin
options.B: Lipase
options.C: Pepsin
options.D: Amylase

explanation: Salivary amylase begins the process of breaking down complex starches into simpler sugars right inside the mouth. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why do we need good 'organising' skills after making a nursing care plan?

options.A: It completely stops all workplace conflicts among nurses
options.B: It eliminates the need for any staff supervision during the shift
options.C: It prevents confusion and resource wastage by defining clear roles
options.D: It guarantees that hospital funding will increase next year

explanation: Great thinking! When you organise well, everyone knows their specific duties for the shift, which stops people from stepping on each other's toes or wasting scarce supplies.

question: What is the biggest perk of insoluble fiber in your digestive system?

options.A: It kills harmful bacteria residing in the stomach lining
options.B: It dissolves completely to lower blood cholesterol levels
options.C: It adds bulk to stool and helps prevent constipation
options.D: It provides quick energy for high-intensity physical exercise

explanation: Insoluble fiber acts like a broom, adding bulk to waste and keeping things moving smoothly so you don't get constipated.

question: A patient refuses a bath because the bathroom feels cold and confusing. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Scold the patient for being uncooperative with personal hygiene
options.B: Cancel all future baths indefinitely to avoid upsetting the patient
options.C: Warm the room, simplify the process, and break it down into gentle steps
options.D: Force the patient into the tub immediately to maintain hygiene standards

explanation: Making the environment cozy and taking things slow helps ease fear and resistance during personal care.

question: Which combination of vital signs points directly to Cushing's triad?

options.A: Widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations
options.B: High fever, hypertension, and excessive sweating
options.C: Hypotension, tachycardia, and normal breathing patterns
options.D: Narrow pulse pressure, tachycardia, and rapid deep breathing

explanation: Cushing's triad is a late, serious sign of high brain pressure. It's the body's desperate, failing attempt to pump blood into a squeezed brain. Great clinical spot!

question: A recovering leprosy patient feels very depressed because people in the community are avoiding them. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise them to pack up and relocate to another state
options.B: Assure them that people will soon forget about it
options.C: Offer a listening ear and connect them with a support group
options.D: Tell the patient never to discuss their illness with anyone

explanation: Emotional support and connecting with others who understand are powerful ways to beat stigma and heal the mind. You're going to be a wonderfully empathetic nurse!

question: Why is advocating for good patient nutrition such a big deal in modern nursing?

options.A: Nurses are required by law to cook meals for every patient
options.B: It generates extra revenue for the hospital administration
options.C: Proper nutrition is essential for preventing and managing chronic diseases
options.D: It replaces the need for administering prescribed medications

explanation: Good food is medicine! Helping patients get the right nutrients speeds up their healing and keeps chronic illnesses under control.

question: Why is regular monitoring of maternal blood pressure important during labor?

options.A: To detect pregnancy-induced hypertension or shock early
options.B: To calculate the exact birth weight of the baby
options.C: To determine when the placenta will separate
options.D: To measure how fast the cervix is opening

explanation: Tracking maternal blood pressure helps identify dangerous spikes like preeclampsia or drops indicating bleeding or distress. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h4)

question: When is the best time to use a multiple line graph?

options.A: When displaying the exact percentages of a single pie chart
options.B: When comparing two or more related trends on the same set of axes
options.C: When listing text instructions for wound dressing changes
options.D: When only a single measurement is taken once in a lifetime

explanation: Correct! When you want to see how two or more groups stack up against each other over the same period, put them on one graph.

question: How can bedside nurses help lower overall health care costs?

options.A: By preventing hospital-acquired complications and minimizing supply waste
options.B: By charging patients directly for bedside nursing procedures
options.C: By eliminating all diagnostic tests from patient care plans
options.D: By shortening physician consultation times during emergencies

explanation: Stopping problems like pressure sores or infections keeps patients safe, out of intensive care, and saves money on wasted supplies.

question: A senior nurse and a junior nurse keep arguing about how to dress a wound. What is this called?

options.A: Intragroup conflict
options.B: Interpersonal conflict
options.C: Organizational conflict
options.D: Intergroup conflict

explanation: When two specific people clash over methods or personalities, it's a classic interpersonal conflict.

question: What is the main job of antibiotics in our bodies?

options.A: To treat and manage bacterial infections
options.B: To boost overall red blood cell counts
options.C: To replace lost fluids and electrolytes
options.D: To lower elevated body temperature rapidly

explanation: You got this! Antibiotics are specifically made to hunt down and stop bacteria from causing trouble in the body. They don't touch viruses or fever on their own!

question: Which of these is a standard single serving of fresh fruit for an adult?

options.A: Five liters of blended fruit smoothie
options.B: One tiny slice of dried pineapple
options.C: Two large bowls of sliced watermelon
options.D: One medium-sized whole orange

explanation: Spot on! One medium-sized whole fruit—like an orange, banana, or apple—makes a perfect single portion.

question: What does it mean when the cervical dilation curve crosses the action line on a partograph?

options.A: The baby is ready to be delivered immediately
options.B: Labor is progressing faster than normal limits
options.C: Intervention or timely referral is urgently required
options.D: The mother has entered the fourth stage of labor

explanation: Crossing the action line signals prolonged labor, prompting healthcare workers to take corrective action or transfer the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h5)

question: Which sign should immediately make a nurse suspect a post-procedure perforation after an esophageal dilation?

options.A: A slight drop in blood pressure after resting
options.B: Sudden severe chest pain and rising heart rate
options.C: Mild sore throat when swallowing saliva
options.D: Low-grade nausea from mild residual sedation

explanation: If a patient suddenly gets severe, worsening chest pain and a fast heart rate (tachycardia), it's a huge red flag that there might be a tear leaking into the chest cavity.

question: What triggers the physical release of milk from the alveoli during breastfeeding?

options.A: Estrogen surge blocking milk ducts
options.B: Progesterone relaxing the nipple sphincter
options.C: Prolactin stopping milk flow temporarily
options.D: Oxytocin causing myoepithelial cell contraction

explanation: Suckling stimulates oxytocin release, which causes the tiny muscle cells around the milk glands to squeeze milk forward. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h1)

question: What effect does severe maternal hypertension or pre-eclampsia typically have on foeto-placental exchange?

options.A: It makes the placental membrane thicker to block toxins
options.B: It increases surface area and speeds up nutrient transfer
options.C: It reduces blood flow and decreases exchange efficiency
options.D: It has no noticeable impact on fetal circulation

explanation: Hypertension causes vessel constriction in the mother's uterus, lowering blood flow to the placenta and starving the fetus of optimal oxygen and nutrients. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h8)

question: Why is a rectovaginal fistula often psychologically distressing for a patient?

options.A: It causes continuous involuntary passage of gas and stool vaginally
options.B: It prevents the patient from ever walking again
options.C: It causes severe upper abdominal pain after meals
options.D: It immediately leads to total kidney failure

explanation: The uncontrollable leakage of feces and flatus through the vagina causes significant hygiene challenges and social embarrassment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: How should a nurse position a patient experiencing Superior Vena Cava Syndrome to help ease their symptoms?

options.A: Flat on their back with no pillow
options.B: With their legs raised higher than their head
options.C: On their left side in the recovery position
options.D: Upright with the head elevated

explanation: Keeping the head of the bed elevated uses gravity to help reduce venous pressure and swelling in the head and neck. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which psychological effect is commonly experienced by individuals undergoing quarantine?

options.A: Anxiety and boredom
options.B: Complete emotional euphoria
options.C: Permanent memory loss
options.D: Increased desire for heavy labor

explanation: Restriction of movement and uncertainty often lead to stress, anxiety, and boredom among confined individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is a common result of supportive and transformational leadership on a hospital ward?

options.A: More communication breakdowns among health workers
options.B: Higher rates of preventable patient falls
options.C: Increased staff turnover and frequent nurse burnout
options.D: Lower medication errors and higher staff satisfaction

explanation: Supportive leadership builds a safe reporting culture and teamwork, which reduces errors and keeps nurses happy. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which surgical treatment uses plates and screws attached directly to the bone to fix a fracture?

options.A: Open reduction internal fixation
options.B: Closed manual manipulation
options.C: External pin stabilization
options.D: Skin traction therapy

explanation: We call this ORIF! The surgeon opens the site to see the bone clearly, then uses internal hardware like metal plates and screws to hold everything tightly in place.

question: When is incidence density preferred over regular cumulative incidence?

options.A: When every single patient is followed for the exact same number of years
options.B: When the researcher wants to measure total existing chronic cases
options.C: When the population size remains completely frozen with zero movement
options.D: When participants enter a study at different times or drop out early

explanation: Real life is messy—people join studies late or drop out. Incidence density handles these rolling timelines like a champ.

question: How does health education in the community help reduce malaria cases?

options.A: It empowers families to use preventive tools and seek early testing
options.B: It replaces the need for hospital laboratories in rural zones
options.C: It provides immediate immunity to newborns in endemic regions
options.D: It permanently eliminates mosquito breeding sites nationwide

explanation: Well done! Teaching families how to use nets properly and report fevers early stops infections before they spiral out of control.

question: Which nutritional deficiency significantly increases a patient's risk of getting pressure sores?

options.A: Protein deficiency
options.B: Sodium overload
options.C: Vitamin C excess
options.D: Carbohydrate restriction

explanation: Protein is like the building blocks for healthy skin. Without enough protein, the skin becomes weak, fragile, and takes forever to repair itself! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why does the body have nerve plexuses (networks of mixed nerves)?

options.A: To separate pain signals before they reach the brain
options.B: To make fluid that protects the spinal cord roots
options.C: To mix nerve fibers so one minor injury doesn't totally paralyze a whole limb
options.D: To create electrical sparks without the spinal cord

explanation: Great job! Plexuses act like backup generator networks, ensuring that a single injury won't knock out movement in an entire arm or leg.

question: Why should you avoid using cold compresses to treat pain during a sickle cell crisis?

options.A: Refrigerated items increase the risk of skin breakdown over swollen joints
options.B: Cold temperatures cause blood vessels to constrict and promote further sickling
options.C: Low temperatures stop intravenous pain medications from working properly
options.D: Cold packs numb the skin so the patient cannot feel if the pain is improving

explanation: Remember: cold makes blood vessels narrow (vasoconstriction). This slows down blood flow even more, making the sickled cells clump together worse and increasing the patient's pain.

question: What is the main difference between primary and secondary skin lesions?

options.A: Primary lesions require surgical removal, while secondary lesions always resolve without any intervention
options.B: Primary lesions only appear on the face, while secondary lesions are found exclusively on the lower extremities
options.C: Primary lesions are always painless, whereas secondary lesions always cause severe systemic fever
options.D: Primary lesions develop directly from the disease process, while secondary ones result from changes like scratching or healing

explanation: You got it! Primary lesions pop up straight from the illness itself, while secondary ones form later due to things like scratching or scabbing.

question: Why is the protein-digesting enzyme pepsin first released in an inactive form called pepsinogen?

options.A: To ensure it only activates when it mixes with bile in the large intestine
options.B: To help the stomach absorb large amounts of water before digestion starts
options.C: To prevent the enzyme from digesting the protein structures of the cells that produce it
options.D: To allow it to travel safely through the bloodstream without breaking down fats

explanation: It's a smart safety feature! If stomach cells made active pepsin right away, the enzyme would turn around and digest the very cells that created it.

question: Why is knowing about negative feedback helpful in nursing care?

options.A: It proves hormones only work through nerves.
options.B: It explains why a struggling gland often causes the brain to pump out more stimulating hormones.
options.C: It means nurses never have to check lab results.
options.D: It keeps blood sugar high during exercise.

explanation: Brilliant! Because of negative feedback, if a target gland fails, the brain tries harder by sending out more stimulating hormones to compensate.

question: What is a must-have when introducing a complex new clinical workflow?

options.A: Protected time for staff training during working hours
options.B: Cutting down the number of patient admissions
options.C: Firing senior nurses to save on salaries
options.D: Buying luxury furniture for the breakroom

explanation: Exactly! You can't expect nurses to master new workflows on top of an already crazy shift without giving them dedicated time to learn.

question: When is transformational leadership most helpful in a healthcare facility?

options.A: When locking ward doors at the end of visiting hours
options.B: During major quality improvement projects and cultural changes
options.C: When calculating monthly payroll and staff tax deductions
options.D: Strictly during immediate, life-threatening cardiac arrests

explanation: When the hospital or ward needs a positive culture shift or new improvements, transformational leaders shine by rallying everyone together.

question: Why is potassium iodide used less often than guaifenesin as an expectorant?

options.A: It turns respiratory secretions completely solid instead of thinning them
options.B: It requires careful monitoring due to potential effects on the thyroid gland
options.C: It can only be administered through direct injection into the bone marrow
options.D: It completely stops all patient movement and causes heavy sedation

explanation: Spot on. Because iodide can mess with the thyroid gland if used for too long, nurses prefer safer options like guaifenesin.

question: Why do large family sizes still hold a lot of cultural importance in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policies mandate a minimum number of children per household.
options.B: Modern contraceptives are completely unavailable in rural areas.
options.C: They are viewed as a symbol of wealth and ancestral continuity.
options.D: Traditional healers require large families for spiritual protection.

explanation: Exactly! In many traditional settings, having a large family is celebrated as a sign of prosperity, strength, and keeping the family lineage alive.

question: What is a simple, practical habit to ensure a patient gets a wide variety of helpful antioxidants and plant nutrients?

options.A: Eating a colorful variety of different fruits and vegetables every day
options.B: Eating the exact same single vegetable for every meal to track intake
options.C: Choosing only white and beige foods because they digest more easily
options.D: Relying entirely on multi-vitamin pills while avoiding fresh produce

explanation: Spot on! Different plant colors mean different health-boosting compounds, so eating a rainbow is always the best prescription.

question: Oh no! A scrub nurse receives a broken suture needle from the surgeon. What should they do first?

options.A: Ask the surgeon to replace the needle holder
options.B: Wait until the end of the operation to mention the break
options.C: Ensure all pieces of the broken needle are accounted for
options.D: Throw the broken pieces into the general waste bin

explanation: You are learning fast! Every single piece of a broken sharp must be found right away so nothing is left inside the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h2)

question: What kind of infectious agent causes Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD)?

options.A: A slow-acting bacterial spore
options.B: An abnormally folded prion protein
options.C: A parasitic protozoan in brain tissue
options.D: A mutant strand of DNA virus

explanation: Spot on! CJD is caused by prions, which are unique proteins that misfold and don't even carry DNA or RNA. You've got this!

question: Which nutrient is especially critical for adolescent girls and boys during major growth spurts to support expanding blood volume?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Fiber
options.D: Iron

explanation: Iron is a core component of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood, making it vital during rapid adolescent growth. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h2)

question: What must a participant give before answering a research questionnaire?

options.A: Proof of health insurance
options.B: A physician's referral letter
options.C: A notarized identity card
options.D: Informed consent

explanation: Participants must voluntarily agree to take part after being fully informed about the study's purpose. Ethical nursing practice starts here!

question: Why is picking the right research design so important for patient care?

options.A: It ensures findings can be trusted and safely applied to patients
options.B: It guarantees that the study will be published in a major journal
options.C: It completely eliminates the possibility of human error
options.D: It reduces the time needed to collect patient data to zero

explanation: When we pick a solid research design, we get reliable evidence. That way, we can make safe, smart decisions right at the patient's bedside with confidence.

question: What do we call the mild, short-lived mood swings and crying spells many women feel right after giving birth?

options.A: Bipolar disorder
options.B: Postpartum psychosis
options.C: Baby blues
options.D: Chronic clinical depression

explanation: Great job! The 'baby blues' are super common, driven by sudden hormone drops and tiredness, and they usually pass within two weeks without needing heavy treatment.

question: What critical warning signs should a nurse teach a post-abortion client before she leaves the clinic?

options.A: Slight breast tenderness in the morning
options.B: Severe pelvic pain, heavy bleeding, or high fever
options.C: A temporary change in her favorite foods
options.D: Mild fatigue and slight spotting for two days

explanation: These symptoms are red flags that can indicate infection, retained tissue, or other complications requiring immediate medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: What three main symptoms usually point toward Meniere's disease?

options.A: Itching, redness, and external swelling
options.B: Fever, ear pain, and purulent drainage
options.C: Total deafness, blindness, and paralysis
options.D: Vertigo, tinnitus, and hearing loss

explanation: Correct! Meniere's is linked to inner ear fluid trouble, bringing on sudden dizziness (vertigo), ringing in the ears (tinnitus), and hearing changes.

question: What is the most important thing a nurse must make clear during pre-vasectomy counseling?

options.A: Sperm analysis is optional after the first month
options.B: The procedure is intended to be permanent
options.C: General anesthesia will be used in the operating room
options.D: Sexual performance will improve after surgery

explanation: Great job! Patients need to know that a vasectomy is meant to be permanent because reversing it is difficult and costly.

question: What is the first practical step a person should take when starting a weekly meal plan?

options.A: Visiting the local market without a list
options.B: Throwing away all existing canned goods
options.C: Ordering takeout food for the upcoming weekend
options.D: Checking current pantry and refrigerator inventory

explanation: Checking what is already at home prevents buying duplicate items and helps build meals around existing ingredients. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h4)

question: When is the best time for a nurse to mark tally sheets for services given?

options.A: Only when requested by visiting supervisors
options.B: Once a week during the staff review meeting
options.C: At the end of the month before submitting reports
options.D: Concurrently or immediately as each patient service is delivered

explanation: Tally as you go! Waiting until the end of a long, tiring shift means you'll definitely forget some numbers.

question: What is the role of the ductus venosus in the baby's abdomen?

options.A: It filters all waste products out of the liver cells
options.B: It supplies the liver with all the baby's red blood cells
options.C: It pumps bile directly from the liver into the umbilical cord
options.D: It allows most oxygenated blood to bypass the liver's capillaries

explanation: Think of the ductus venosus as a VIP bypass lane around the liver, rushing rich oxygen straight to the heart without getting slowed down. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h5)

question: Why is it best practice for nurses to involve community leaders when planning health programs?

options.A: It prevents NGOs from ever visiting rural communities
options.B: It fosters local ownership and reduces cultural resistance to care
options.C: It removes the need for nurses to document patient treatments
options.D: It ensures that healthcare providers receive financial bonuses

explanation: When local leaders are part of the plan, the community feels respected, trusts the process, and joins in willingly.

question: What is the primary goal of routine HIV testing during antenatal care (PMTCT programs)?

options.A: To prevent transmission of the virus from mother to child
options.B: To replace standard antenatal blood pressure checks
options.C: To determine eligibility for paid maternity leave benefits
options.D: To enforce mandatory quarantine for pregnant women

explanation: You nailed it! Testing mums early lets them start treatment so they can drastically lower the chance of passing the virus to their baby.

question: Why is quitting smoking considered 'primary prevention' rather than 'secondary prevention'?

options.A: It is only performed after a patient receives a confirmed cancer diagnosis.
options.B: It relies entirely on surgical removal of damaged bronchial tissue.
options.C: It focuses on finding small tumors before symptoms appear.
options.D: It aims to prevent the disease from ever developing in the first place.

explanation: Brilliant! Primary prevention stops harmful exposures (like tobacco) so the disease process never even gets a chance to start.

question: What is the primary requirement for a safe home delivery?

options.A: Having family members present
options.B: Taking herbal medications daily
options.C: Strict screening and careful planning
options.D: Living close to a major market

explanation: Home delivery is only safe when there is careful planning and proper screening to identify low-risk candidates beforehand. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is a common mistake when looking at a significant Chi-Square result?

options.A: Assuming statistical significance proves strong clinical importance
options.B: Expecting the sample size to decrease automatically
options.C: Believing that the expected frequencies must equal zero
options.D: Thinking the test can only be used with continuous numerical data

explanation: Good catch! A result can be statistically significant, but you still have to use clinical judgment to see if it makes a big real-world difference for patients.

question: What happens to blood volume when sodium levels rise in the blood?

options.A: Blood volume drops rapidly through increased sweating
options.B: Blood volume decreases because sodium repels water
options.C: Blood volume stays the same because cells absorb the excess
options.D: Blood volume increases because water follows sodium

explanation: Sodium exerts strong osmotic pressure, meaning water is drawn toward areas with higher sodium concentration, thereby increasing total fluid volume. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h2)

question: Why is communication considered a two-way process in the IEC framework?

options.A: It focuses only on passing medical news from the hospital to the village
options.B: It requires two different nurses to speak at the same community meeting
options.C: It means printing health materials in both English and a local language
options.D: It involves listening to community feedback and addressing local fears

explanation: Effective communication in IEC goes beyond just giving orders; it requires listening to what the community has to say and clearing up doubts. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h1)

question: A voluntary agency sets up a mobile clinic in a remote village with no hospital. What core function are they carrying out?

options.A: Commercial pharmaceutical manufacturing
options.B: Direct health service delivery
options.C: Conducting forensic autopsies
options.D: Enforcing health legislation

explanation: Well done! Bringing doctors, nurses, and treatments straight to people in remote areas is direct health service delivery.

question: How do cultural expectations in Nigeria often worsen the emotional strain of male infertility?

options.A: Society places heavy emphasis on fatherhood and family lineage, leading to deep personal stigma
options.B: Cultural practices strictly forbid men from undergoing any form of medical testing
options.C: Traditional healers are legally required to manage all reproductive health conditions
options.D: Communities automatically blame the female partner, protecting the man from stress

explanation: The strong cultural expectation to bear children creates intense psychological pressure and shame when fertility challenges arise. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h8)

question: What type of observation happens when a researcher joins a group to experience their daily routine firsthand?

options.A: Non-participant observation
options.B: Participant observation
options.C: Structured observation
options.D: Laboratory observation

explanation: You got it! In 'participant observation', the researcher actively joins the community to get an inside perspective.

question: Which member of the hospice team primarily helps families navigate financial and social resource planning?

options.A: The medical social worker
options.B: The hospice facility chaplain
options.C: The attending medical physician
options.D: The certified nursing assistant

explanation: Social workers are trained to help families manage financial concerns, legal documents, and community support resources. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h4)

question: What is a frequent cause of severe injuries on industrial cargo or work boats?

options.A: Falling debris from land-based skyscrapers
options.B: Sudden attacks by wild marine mammals on deck
options.C: Machinery entanglements and heavy winch failures
options.D: High-speed motor vehicle collisions at sea

explanation: Correct! Industrial ships have heavy gears and winches that can unfortunately cause serious mechanical injuries to the crew.

question: Why is involving men in family health beneficial for the household?

options.A: It improves health outcomes for women and children
options.B: It reduces the household income requirement
options.C: It makes clinic visits shorter for everyone
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses

explanation: Active male participation creates a supportive environment that directly boosts health and wellness for mothers and children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h1)

question: A nurse held two town hall meetings and shared 500 flyers about clean water. To see if the advocacy actually worked (the outcome), what should the nurse check next?

options.A: How many total hours the nurse spent walking to the meeting venues
options.B: How boxes of leaflets were left over in the clinic storage room
options.C: Whether the printer charged a fair market price for the paper used
options.D: Whether the local government committed funds to fix the water source

explanation: You've got it! Handing out flyers is just the activity; seeing if the government actually takes action tells you if your advocacy made a real-world difference.

question: Which nursing action should you AVOID when trying to cool down a patient with a fever?

options.A: Giving prescribed paracetamol
options.B: Putting the patient in an ice-cold bath
options.C: Offering plenty of water to drink
options.D: Keeping the hospital room well-ventilated

explanation: Spot on! Ice-cold water makes the patient shiver violently, which actually pushes their internal temperature back up.

question: A patient wakes up restless, pacing, and yelling after getting a sedative. What is this unexpected reaction called?

options.A: Physical dependence
options.B: Drug tolerance
options.C: Paradoxical reaction
options.D: Allergic anaphylaxis

explanation: A paradoxical reaction is when a drug does the exact opposite of what you expect—making someone hyper instead of calm! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h7)

question: What does we mean when we say there is a disease outbreak?

options.A: The total eradication of a chronic illness from a population
options.B: A sudden rise in disease cases above normal expectations
options.C: Any single confirmed case of a rare tropical infection
options.D: A predictable seasonal spike in common malaria cases

explanation: An outbreak simply means more people are getting sick than we usually see for that time and place. You've got this!

question: Why is a patient in the prodromal stage often a high risk for spreading germs to others?

options.A: Their immune system has completely stopped functioning
options.B: They feel well enough to move around while carrying germs
options.C: They shed the highest volume of toxic waste products
options.D: Pathogens multiply exclusively during this specific phase

explanation: Spot on! Because they don't feel super sick yet, they keep moving around and unknowingly expose people around them.

question: A nurse reviews a high-quality study on a new pain management protocol. What local factor must be checked before introducing it to the ward?

options.A: Whether the ward has the staff training and resources to support the protocol
options.B: How many awards the primary investigator has won
options.C: Whether the original authors will visit the hospital to supervise
options.D: If the journal article has a colorful cover page

explanation: Research implementation must always consider local feasibility, including equipment, staff readiness, and institutional support. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why should nursing leaders join daily safety huddles during a culture change?

options.A: It prevents doctors from questioning the clinical decisions made by nurses
options.B: It proves to staff that leadership values safety and is committed to the change
options.C: It ensures that nurses finish their morning documentation much faster
options.D: It eliminates the need for any further written incident reporting

explanation: Exactly! When leaders 'walk the talk' and show up for frontline safety routines, it builds real trust with the nursing team.

question: What is the primary cause of respiratory acidosis?

options.A: Severe vomiting resulting in the loss of gastric acid
options.B: Renal failure causing a buildup of bicarbonate ions
options.C: Hyperventilation leading to excessive carbon dioxide loss
options.D: Hypoventilation leading to carbon dioxide retention

explanation: If a patient isn't breathing enough (hypoventilation), $CO_2$ piles up in the blood. Because $CO_2$ is an acid, this buildup leads to respiratory acidosis.

question: Why would a nurse place the bell of a stethoscope over an enlarged thyroid gland?

options.A: To listen for a bruit caused by increased blood flow
options.B: To check for crackles moving up from the trachea
options.C: To measure the exact width of the thyroid lobes
options.D: To assess for abnormal whistling breath sounds

explanation: An overactive thyroid sucks up a massive amount of blood. That rushing blood creates an audible whooshing sound called a bruit that you can actually hear through your stethoscope!

question: What happens to a research study if it lacks a clear conceptual framework?

options.A: It stops patients from participating in the project
options.B: It automatically becomes much easier to complete
options.C: It requires fewer ethical approvals from the committee
options.D: It can easily lose focus and gather irrelevant data

explanation: Without a clear map, you might end up collecting tons of information that doesn't actually help answer your research question. Keep it focused!

question: What kind of body cells do cytotoxic drugs attack the most?

options.A: Rapidly dividing cells
options.B: Slow-growing bone cells
options.C: Mature nerve fibers
options.D: Dormant fat tissues

explanation: You've got this! Cytotoxic drugs are designed to target and destroy cells that divide quickly, which is a main feature of cancer cells.

question: What is the term for the unwritten social rules about how men and women should behave?

options.A: Biological sex
options.B: Genetic traits
options.C: Gender norms
options.D: Chromosomal codes

explanation: Gender norms are societal expectations that dictate acceptable behaviors and roles for different genders within a specific culture. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of using a person-centred approach in post-abortion counseling?

options.A: It helps match birth control to the client's unique lifestyle and goals
options.B: It guarantees the patient will never feel any grief
options.C: It speeds up the clinic discharge paperwork
options.D: It forces the client to choose the strongest long-term method

explanation: Person-centred care is all about listening to what the patient wants. When they choose a method that fits their life, they are much happier using it!

question: How do thiazide diuretics and loop diuretics differ in how they handle calcium?

options.A: Thiazides keep all potassium in the body while loop diuretics waste it
options.B: Thiazides increase calcium excretion while loop diuretics decrease it
options.C: Thiazides have no effect on any electrolytes except sodium
options.D: Thiazides decrease calcium excretion while loop diuretics increase it

explanation: Good to know: thiazides help your kidneys hold onto calcium (lowering it in the urine), while loop diuretics cause calcium to be washed out.

question: A patient comes back two days after an abscess drainage with a fever and redness that is spreading outward from the wound. What does this mean?

options.A: Worsening infection requiring prompt medical reassessment
options.B: An allergic reaction to the cotton inside the dressing
options.C: Successful eradication of all bacteria from the body
options.D: Normal healing response as the deep tissues close

explanation: Spreading redness and fever are warning signs that the infection is fighting back and traveling further. The patient needs a doctor to take a look right away.

question: Why is a functional referral network important for big teaching hospitals?

options.A: It eliminates the need for community health nurses altogether
options.B: It guarantees that every patient gets admitted for surgery
options.C: It prevents minor health issues from clogging up specialist care
options.D: It ensures that doctors only work half-day shifts

explanation: When primary clinics handle minor cases and only refer severe ones, tertiary hospitals can focus on complex medical conditions. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h1)

question: What is the primary physiological cause of fainting?

options.A: A sudden temporary drop in blood flow to the brain
options.B: An acute electrical storm in the brain tissue
options.C: A permanent blockage of the carotid arteries
options.D: A severe deficiency of potassium in the blood

explanation: Fainting happens when cerebral blood flow drops briefly, starving the brain of oxygen and glucose. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h1)

question: What does a null hypothesis usually state?

options.A: There is a strong positive effect from the treatment
options.B: There is no relationship between the variables
options.C: The sample size is too small to complete the study
options.D: The research question was poorly written

explanation: The null hypothesis is the 'no difference' or 'no effect' guess. It assumes any change you see is just by chance!

question: What question does a healthcare organization's mission statement primarily answer?

options.A: How many patient beds will we add in twenty years?
options.B: Which staff members deserve a promotion this month?
options.C: Why do we exist right now and who do we serve?
options.D: What will our total financial budget be next year?

explanation: The mission statement defines the current purpose and core activities of the healthcare facility. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why do complication rates from unsafe abortions tend to be higher in villages than in cities?

options.A: Delays in reaching qualified medical help worsen emergency outcomes
options.B: Rural women have better access to sterile surgical instruments
options.C: Traditional healers in villages always use modern antibiotics
options.D: Rural clinics are strictly reserved for reproductive emergencies

explanation: You nailed it. Long travel times mean infections and bleeding go unchecked for too long before reaching a nurse.

question: Why is community education just as important as legal bans when fighting to eliminate FGM?

options.A: Healthcare workers are not allowed to read legal documents
options.B: Community education changes cultural beliefs and tackles the root causes
options.C: Community leaders demand payment to obey the law
options.D: Laws are too expensive to print and distribute

explanation: You got it! While laws set the rules, stopping deep-seated traditions requires educating community members so they choose to leave the practice behind. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h8)
